Sam —

Thanks for the clear list. High level answers below; I'll follow up with an export example and an estimated timeline.

1) What we log
- Interactive console actions (login events, session start/end, MFA challenges), user role and permission changes, API key creation/rotation/revocation, service account activity, system-initiated admin tasks (backups, schema migrations), and operator impersonation events.
- We also capture request metadata (IP, user-agent, region), request IDs, and correlated trace ids when available.

2) Export formats and provenance
- Exports supported: compressed JSONL (newline-delimited JSON), CSV, and Parquet. Each export is accompanied by a signed manifest (SHA-256 checksum) and an export metadata JSON that describes the time range, record count, and schema version.
- We can optionally provide a PGP-signed manifest on request for legal chains of custody.

3) Retention and snapshots
- Default retention for admin activity is 13 months. Shorter windows (90/180/365 days) are available per contract.
- We support point-in-time snapshots: we can produce a manifested bundle for an arbitrary time span (minimum 1 hour) and attest to the extraction time. Snapshots include timezone-normalized ISO timestamps and tenant identifiers for scoping.

4) Delivery options and security controls
- Delivery: S3 PUT to your bucket (SSE-KMS), S3 presigned GET links (time-limited), SFTP push to a specified endpoint, or encrypted HTTP POST to a secure endpoint.
- Key management: we support customer-managed KMS keys (you provide ARN) or Redwood-managed keys; manifests include KMS key ID used for server-side encryption.
- We add HMAC timestamps if you need an additional integrity check layered over the manifest.

Timeline: for a standard evidence bundle (30-day range) we can deliver within 48-72 business hours after request if no redaction is required. For scoped historical snapshots that need redaction, plan for 5-7 business days.

I'll attach a small sample export (JSONL) and a sample signed manifest in my next message. Looping in Karthik for retention SLAs and Marissa for attested delivery procedures.

— Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Head of Trust & Compliance | Redwood Inference

Adding operational detail on retention and redaction: 

- Retention tiers are configurable per-tenant. We can commit to 13 months by default; extended retention (up to 7 years) is available under enterprise contracts with archival S3 tiers.
- PII redaction: exports can be run through a configurable scrubbing pipeline that replaces or nulls fields (email, IP last octet, device ids) per your redaction policy. We track redaction in the manifest (redaction_policy_id and redaction_version).
- Integrity: exports are checksummed (SHA-256) and stored with an HMAC using a rotating key; attestation artifacts (signed timestamp, export-runner-id) are embedded in the metadata file.
- Access controls: export requests require an authorized ticket (we can accept DocuSign/PSA proof of request) and are audited as privileged operations.

Operational SLA example:
- On-demand snapshot (non-redacted): 48 hours
- Historical snapshot > 90 days (redaction required): 5 business days

I'll coordinate with Marissa on packaging the sample bundle and the signed manifest.

Karthik

Quick checklist we follow for evidence delivery: 
- Confirm scope and time range
- Verify requestor authorization (POC + signed intake form)
- Select retention/redaction profile and snapshot window
- Generate export, compute checksums, create signed manifest, package bundle
- Deliver via agreed transport (customer S3 bucket preferred) and post-delivery verification (receipt+checksum)
